id_and_class.summary: François Kammerer defends strong illusionism: phenomenal consciousness does not exist but only seems to, because introspection represents our states as phenomenal. His TCE theory explains why the illusion is so compelling, and Kammerer argues that illusionism defends physicalism better than its standard versions do.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Phenomenal Consciousness as a Product of Introspective Misrepresentation

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Phenomenal consciousness is nothing; what exists is the appearance of it, produced when introspection applies phenomenal concepts to our states.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Everything is physical. Kammerer holds that the popular defenses of physicalism against anti-physicalist arguments fail, and that denying the existence of phenomenal states removes the premise those arguments need.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable (phenomenal consciousness does not exist, so it is neither primitive nor emergent)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Our naïve theory of mind includes a naïve epistemology that treats phenomenal states as epistemologically special, known in a uniquely direct way. That built-in assumption is what makes the illusion feel undeniable.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Phenomenal properties, the qualia of pain, color, or joy, are never instantiated. We believe in them because we represent them introspectively.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Physical states and the introspective processes and concepts that represent them, including phenomenal concepts that misrepresent.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Introspection gives non-inferential beliefs about our experiences, but those beliefs are systematically mistaken about phenomenality.

mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: The TCE theory: phenomenal introspection applies phenomenal concepts, which are Theoretically determined Concepts of Epistemologically special states.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Introspection represents our own states as phenomenal, using concepts fixed by a naïve theory of mind rather than by what the states are.
core_claims_and_evidence: Phenomenal consciousness does not exist but seems to exist.
A good theory of introspection must explain both why consciousness seems to exist and why we cannot intuitively make sense of its not existing.
Existing theories of introspection cannot do this job; TCE theory is meant to.
David Chalmers’s ‘Moorean’ argument fails because its key premise cannot be supported without begging the question against illusionism.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Philosophical, drawing on philosophy of mind and cognitive science of introspection.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: The main objection is that illusionism is obviously false, since it is evident that we have experiences; Chalmers puts this as a Moorean argument. Kammerer grants that the view is radically counter-intuitive and may even seem incoherent, but argues that the illusion itself predicts that resistance.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Kammerer admits that explaining why the illusion of phenomenality is so peculiar is no trivial task. The normative consequences of illusionism, while not as gloomy as some fear, may be hard to deal with.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Consistent with physicalism, which Kammerer argues illusionism serves better than its rivals.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Since only physical states exist and phenomenal consciousness is an illusion, nothing nonphysical remains to survive death.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Kammerer argues that things can still have value if phenomenal consciousness does not exist, but admits the normative consequences can be difficult to deal with.

sources_and_references.title_with_names: Kammerer’s Introspective Illusionism (Landscape of Consciousness), François Kammerer
